boardCostEvidence.claim: Autoliv 77 GHz radar teardown report includes an estimate of PCB cost (figure not public).
Radar RF board is costly; hybrid PTFE/FR4 asymmetric substrate with a planar antenna hard to produce; substrate a major part of RF-board cost (reseller listing of a 12-radar study).
Hybrid builds (FR4 + RF-optimised laminate) lower system cost v all-RF; RF laminates' high CTE risks delamination in thermal cycling.
Rogers offers RO4830 thermoset as a cost-effective option to optimise performance and total cost; RO3003/RO3003G2 for 77 GHz antennas, RO4835 for 24 GHz.
RO3003G2: Dk 3.07 at 77 GHz, 1.3 dB/inch insertion loss (5 mil) — for ACC, FCW, BSD, park pilot.
Patent: waveguide antenna lets the radar PCB use standard inexpensive FR4 instead of specialty RF laminate.

notes: No public numeric figure was found for a board's cost or for the RF-laminate premium; the teardown reports that hold them (Yole/System Plus, Research and Markets) are paywalled.
No teardown found states a layer count, board size or surface finish for any production ADAS board; those fields are engineering judgement or 'not published'.
4D radar (beyond ARS540's processor), park-assist/ultrasonic and LiDAR were not researched: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task. Re-run for these.
TechInsights' Bosch MPC3 summary describes L8B2-14F404 as a Land Rover Defender night-vision module; treat MPC3 IC list as that unit's.
SVC board size is from a TI reference design, not a production teardown.
Tesla HW4 board facts come from TechInsights summaries and secondary reports of greentheonly's photos; HW3 memory list may include non-FSD parts of the unit.
